author: Brother Ilvaren of the Chapel of Akatosh
pages:
#The Night of Fire

My grandfather's grandfather was a boy in Kvatch when the gates of Oblivion opened outside the walls. He remembered the sky turning the color of a wound, and the things that walked out of the light.

Kvatch burned in a single night. Almost no one got out.

#The Hero

One stranger went into the gate and came out again, holding a stone that pulsed like a heart. The gate fell in on itself. The siege broke.

We never learned the stranger's name for certain. The chapel keeps a statue with no face, and every child in Kvatch knows who it is.

#Rebuilding

Kvatch was rebuilt stone by stone over a hundred years. The new walls are thicker. The chapel bell rings at dusk, every dusk, to remind the hills that the city is still awake.

Some nights, shepherds say the hills above the city hum. We ring the bell a little louder.
